# WindowsMidiServices (module)

This external module does **not** bundle any Microsoft files. It points at the Windows MIDI Services
(`Windows.Devices.Midi2`, in-box API preview) C++/WinRT projection and runtime that the **host project**
supplies, and compiles the Windows MIDI Services backend of libremidi in only when they are found.

## Required layout (in the host project, not in this plugin)

```
<Project>/ThirdParty/WindowsMidiServices/
  Win64/
    include/
      winrt/
        base.h                                 (C++/WinRT, same cppwinrt run as everything below)
        Windows.Devices.Midi2*.h, Windows.Foundation*.h, Windows.Devices*.h, Windows.Storage*.h, impl/...
      WindowsMidiServicesAppSdkComExtensions.h (optional: raw endpoint connection fast path)
    bin/
      Windows.Devices.Midi2.dll
      Windows.Devices.Midi2.pri
  metadata/
    Windows.Devices.Midi2.winmd                (not used by the build; kept with the projection)
  VERSION.txt                                  (which Microsoft build the files are from)
```

The projection must be a **matched set** generated by a single `cppwinrt.exe` run (including `winrt/base.h`
and the whole dependency closure of the Midi2 headers, not just the Midi2 headers): every generated header
asserts the exact C++/WinRT version, and the Windows SDK that Unreal selects may carry an older cppwinrt.

## Behaviour

- `Win64/include/winrt/Windows.Devices.Midi2.h` and `winrt/base.h` found: `WITH_WINDOWS_MIDI_SERVICES=1`,
  `include` is added as a system include path, and `LIBREMIDI_WINMIDI` is defined (see `libremidi.Build.cs`).
- `bin/Windows.Devices.Midi2.dll` and `.pri` are added as runtime dependencies (staged loose at the same
  project-relative path in packaged builds). The `Libremidi4UE` module preloads the DLL by full path at startup.
- Not found, or no project file (engine-only target): `WITH_WINDOWS_MIDI_SERVICES=0`, a build warning says where
  to put the files, and only WinMM (MIDI 1.0) is available on Windows.

After adding or removing the files, touch a `.Build.cs` (or rebuild) so that UnrealBuildTool re-evaluates the
detection; it can reuse a cached makefile otherwise.

The Microsoft files are subject to Microsoft's own license terms for the release you take them from.
Do not commit them to the public Libremidi4UE repository.
